subject: Post-call: context footprint and per-1M pricing windows
thread_text:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <dan.cho@novacorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: context footprint and per-1M pricing windows

Thanks again for the call this morning, Daniel — good discussion. Below is a concise recap plus the asks we agreed on so we can align pricing and recommend the right context tier.

Quick recap (what we heard)
- Primary product flows: search & retrieval augmentation (low latency), analytics summarization (mid latency), and monthly large-batch document transforms for compliance reporting.
- Expected monthly token footprint (initial): 50M — 150M tokens. Growth depends on expansion into analytics flows.
- Observed per-request profile from your sample: average prompt tokens ~320, average completion tokens ~1,300. Distribution estimate: ~60% short outputs (<=512 tokens), ~30% medium (512–4k), ~10% long (>4k).
- Context depth needs:
  - 8k window: baseline for most search/augmentation requests (core usage).
  - 32k window: needed for multi-doc analytics and longer summarization.
  - 128k window: occasional (estimated 3–7% of calls) for full-document transforms and legal compliance exports.

Primary asks from Novacorp
1) Baseline per-1M token price targets they'd consider acceptable (range).
2) A short pricing scenarios sheet for: pay-as-you-go hosted, 12-month reserved capacity, and a pilot reserved bundle (3 months).
3) Security checklist / SOC2 + audit-log evidence and confirmation that uploads are encrypted in transit and at rest.

What we need from Novacorp to finalize scenarios
- Confirm expected % of requests in the 128k bucket (we have 3–7% from today’s sample — ask you to confirm whether that scales with production).
- Any SLA/throughput commitments for peak windows (e.g., sustained 200 qps during business hours?).
- Preferred procurement cadence (PO now vs. invoiced contract).

Next steps (proposal)
- We will send a 1-page pricing scenarios sheet + a short pilot scope by EOD tomorrow.
- Suggested follow-up: 30m call next Wed to walk numbers with procurement and engineering.

Attachments: novacorp-context-samples.csv (sample profile), pricing-scenarios-1M.xlsx (working scenarios), redwood-security-summary.pdf (SOC2 + logs overview).

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

---

From: Daniel Cho <dan.cho@novacorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: context footprint and per-1M pricing windows

Thanks, Rachel — appreciate the summary. A few clarifying points so the scenarios line up with our procurement expectations:
- The average completion tokens I quoted on the call was conservative for long jobs; for our largest summarizations the average completion can be closer to ~2,000 tokens, so please size the 128k examples with a slightly higher completion average.
- Our compliance team will require SOC2 Type II evidence and a sample of audit logs for token-level request IDs; can you include a redacted sample in the bundle?
- Procurement is targeting a target list price around $700–$900 per 1M tokens for our committed volume (50–150M), but we understand long-window calls have higher unit cost. Would like three scenario buckets: 1) no commitment / hosted PAYG, 2) 12-mo commit (min 75M/mo), 3) pilot (3 months, up to 20M tokens) with credits for evaluation.

Can we do a follow-up Wed 9/22 10am PT to walk procurement + eng?

Daniel
Director of Product, Novacorp
dan.cho@novacorp.com | +1 212-555-0134

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <dan.cho@novacorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: context footprint and per-1M pricing windows

Daniel — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is the pricing-scenarios-1M.xlsx and a short notes doc in the CSV that summarizes the sample we pulled and the assumptions used. Highlights from our side (quick read):

Pricing scenarios (high level — per 1M input+output tokens, illustrative):
- Scenario A — Hosted PAYG (no commitment)
  - 8k window: $620 per 1M tokens
  - 32k window: $1,020 per 1M tokens
  - 128k window: $1,750 per 1M tokens
  - Notes: good for bursty evaluation; no commitment discount; on-demand performance with standard rate limits.

- Scenario B — 12-mo reserved (committed capacity, blended)
  - Effective blended pricing (for 50–150M/mo profile): $520 per 1M (8k), $880 per 1M (32k), $1,450 per 1M (128k)
  - Notes: includes 10–20% reserved discount, priority routing, and 99.9% uptime SLA.

- Scenario C — Pilot bundle (3 months, up to 20M tokens)
  - Blended pilot price: $460 per 1M (8k), $780 per 1M (32k), $1,100 per 1M (128k)
  - Includes a $10k credit if pilot metrics (latency & correctness) meet agreed targets; limited to hosted instances.

Unit economics commentary (what the costs reflect)
- The per-1M figures above incorporate: run-time GPU compute, KV cache effectiveness on repeated prefixes (we assumed 12% token-level cache hit on the sample), batching efficiency for your 60/30/10 distribution, and overhead for longer-context kernel selection.
- For your expected 50–150M monthly volume, the blended reserved scenario should reduce unit cost materially vs PAYG — the biggest lever is committing to a portion of long-window capacity.

Security / compliance
- redwood-security-summary.pdf (attached) contains SOC2 summary, a sample redacted audit log export, and KMS integration notes. For procurement: we can provide a limited audit-log export and a SOC2 Type II report under NDA.

Next steps (from our side)
1) If you confirm the 128k call percentage (3–7% vs higher), we’ll finalize a more precise blended price sheet and an initial contract SOW.
2) I’ll add a one-page pilot SOW and a proposed measurement plan (latency, success-rate, and correctness) to the Drive folder.
3) Proposed follow-up: Wed 9/22 10am PT with procurement + eng to walk the scenarios.

If that works, I’ll send calendar invites and drop the final XLS in the Drive link.

Best,
Rachel

Nice write-up. Internal notes / ask:
- Push the pilot SOW with the $10k credit and a 3-week evaluation window; include 3 clear pass/fail gating metrics (latency P95 < 450ms for 8k, correctness > 92% on eval set, and stable throughput for 32k flows).
- For the 12-mo reserved, draft two commitment bands: 75M/mo and 125M/mo with escalator discounts at renewal.
- Sales motion: propose a one-week free technical onboarding credit (zero-cost capacity) for engineering to ingest initial dataset (helps reduce friction).

Ben / Rachel — can you prepare the pilot SOW + a concise line-item pricing sheet tomorrow so we can land the follow-up with procurement on 9/22?

Karthik
VP, Product Engineering | Redwood Inference
